TryfundableAPIKeyCredential.title: Tryfundable API Key
TryfundableAPIKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: Paste your Fundable API key from API Access. Requests use Authorization: Bearer. Connection testing reads your own alert configurations without spending credits and requires a Pro+ or Enterprise plan; other keys may be saved as unverified. Discovery and contact unlocks consume credits according to your plan.

TryfundableGetAlertsConfig.description:
Retrieve saved alert data including all deals that matched the alert criteria within the specified date range.
Results include a flattened array of deals sorted by date (newest first) with duplicates removed.

Available on Pro+ and Enterprise plans. This endpoint does not consume credits.

**Multiple Alerts Support:**
- Query multiple alerts in a single request (up to 10)
- Each alert returns its own flattened deals array
- Different alerts can have different frequencies (e.g., one daily, one weekly)
- Successful requests report `credits_used: 0`, regardless of deal count

**Important Notes:**
- All alert_ids must belong to alerts you have access to
- Deals are flattened from all time periods and sorted by date DESC (newest first)
- Duplicate deals are automatically removed
- Each deal includes AI-generated reasoning for why it matched the alert criteria
- Deal structure is simplified with flattened company information for easier integration

alert_ids.description:
Comma-separated list of alert UUIDs (up to 10 alerts per request).
All alerts must be associated with your API key's account.
Example: "uuid1,uuid2,uuid3"
alert_ids.title: Alert Ids

start_date.description:
Start date for the alert data range (ISO 8601 format).
Results will include deals from this date onwards.
start_date.title: Start Date

end_date.description:
End date for the alert data range (ISO 8601 format).
Results will include deals up to and including this date.

**Note:** All dates are processed in UTC timezone. Deals are grouped into time periods based on UTC date boundaries.
end_date.title: End Date

TryfundableGetCompanyConfig.description:
Use this endpoint when one company is already identified and its full profile and
latest funding round are required. Prefer a domain or LinkedIn URL when available;
they can be passed directly here without calling `/company/search` first.

Use `/company/search` for fuzzy company-name resolution or an uncertain identifier.
Use `POST /companies` to discover or batch-retrieve multiple companies.

Provide ONE of the following query parameters to identify the company:
- `id` - Company UUID
- `domain` - Company domain or full URL (e.g., "stripe.com" or "https://stripe.com")
- `linkedin` - LinkedIn company URL
- `crunchbase` - Crunchbase organization URL

The response includes the company's latest funding round details with participating investors.

domain.title: Domain

TryfundableGetCompanyDealsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint when a company is already identified and its complete funding
history is required. Prefer a domain or LinkedIn URL when available; it can be
passed directly without first calling `/company/search`.

This route retrieves history for one identified company. Use `POST /deals` instead
to discover rounds across the market with deal, company, or investor filters.

Provide ONE of the following query parameters to identify the company:
- `id` - Company UUID
- `domain` - Company domain or full URL (e.g., "stripe.com" or "https://stripe.com")
- `linkedin` - LinkedIn company URL
- `crunchbase` - Crunchbase organization URL

The response includes the company's deals with pagination. If the identifier matches multiple companies, deals from all matches are returned.

TryfundableGetDealInvestorsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint after identifying a deal when investor IDs in the deal record
need to be resolved into the complete investor lineup. It returns firm investors,
associated people, angel investors, lead status, and profile links for one deal.

Do not use this endpoint to discover investors across many deals. Use
`POST /investors` when the desired result is a list of firms, or `POST /people`
with investor filters when the desired result is individual investors.

Use `POST /investors` instead to discover firms from investment criteria, or
`POST /deals` when the desired result is a filtered list of funding rounds.

TryfundableListAlertConfigurationsConfig.description:
Retrieve all alert configurations for the authenticated user (identified by API key).
Returns configuration metadata including filters, frequency, and descriptions.

Available on Pro+ and Enterprise plans. This endpoint does not consume credits.

**Important Notes:**
- This endpoint does NOT consume usage credits (actualUsageCount: 0)
- Returns only configuration metadata, not deal data
- Does not require any query parameters - user is identified by API key
- All configurations for the authenticated user are returned (no pagination)

**Authentication:**
- User identity is automatically determined from the API key
- No email or user_id parameter needed

**Use Cases:**
- Look up what alerts are configured for the authenticated user
- Retrieve alert filter settings for external integrations
- Audit alert configurations programmatically
TryfundableListAlertConfigurationsConfig.title: TryfundableListAlertConfigurationsConfig

TryfundableListInvestorsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint when the requested result is a list of investor firms. Filters
under `company_investments` identify qualifying portfolio companies and deals, then
return the firms that participated in those deals. For example, use this route to
find San Francisco-based investors that participated in a Seed round during the
last year.

Use `POST /people` with investor filters instead when the desired result is an
individual angel investor or lead partner attached to a firm. Use `POST /deals`
when the desired result is the matching funding rounds themselves.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 3 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific investors by UUID, domain, LinkedIn, or Crunchbase
- `investor` - Filter by investor entity attributes (location, employee count)
- `company_investments` - Filter by portfolio (industries, deal characteristics, etc.). Supports semantic search via `search_query` + `min_relevance`.

When `company_investments` filters are active, `filtered_deal_count` is the number
of deals that matched those filters and `filtered_lead_count` is the number of those
matched deals the investor led.

company_investments.description: Portfolio filters (filter by companies the investor has invested in)

sort_by.description:
Sort order for results.
- **most_recent_deal** — Date of most recent investment (newest first)
- **recent_deals** — Deals in last 12 months (highest first)
- **deals_led_ltm** — Lead deals in last 12 months (highest first)
- **total_deals** — All-time deal count (highest first)
- **matching_deals** — Deals matching portfolio filters (highest first)
sort_by.title: Sort By

search_query.description:
AI-powered semantic search matched against each investor's
portfolio companies — a flexible replacement for an industry tag.
First use /industry/search and apply an `industries` or
`super_categories` filter when the taxonomy contains the intended
category. Use semantic search only for a niche industry or specific
product type the taxonomy cannot express, describing what those
companies do — their product, technology, or business model (e.g.
"climate-focused carbon capture hardware"). Do NOT use it for other
attributes like stage, location, or funding — apply those with the
dedicated `company_investments` and `investor` filter fields instead.
Results are ranked by portfolio relevance and capped at 150 semantic
matches.
search_query.title: Search Query

min_relevance.description:
Minimum relevance score threshold (0–1) for the portfolio-based
semantic search. Only applies when `search_query` is provided.
Investors whose portfolio match score falls below this threshold
are excluded. Defaults to 0 (return all results).
min_relevance.title: Min Relevance

TryfundableSearchCompaniesConfig.description:
Use this endpoint by default for company sourcing and discovery. It returns company
metadata such as name and domain together with the full details of each company's
latest funding round.

Filters inside `latest_deal` apply only to the company's most recent round. Use
`POST /deals` instead when deal criteria must match any round in a company's history.
For example, `/companies` is appropriate for "find AI companies in San Francisco
whose latest round was Seed"; `/deals` is appropriate for "analyze all Seed rounds
announced last year," regardless of whether Seed is now the company's latest round.

Filters inside `investors` can match investor participation across all rounds.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific companies by UUID, domain, LinkedIn, or Crunchbase
- `company` - Filter by company attributes (search, location, industry, size, etc.)
- `latest_deal` - Filter by latest funding round attributes (type, size, date, investors)
- `investors` - Filter by investors (firms or people) across all rounds

investors.description: Filter by investors (firms or people) across all funding rounds

TryfundableSearchCompanyConfig.description:
Use this endpoint primarily to resolve a fuzzy company name or an uncertain
identifier into matching company records. If a reliable domain or LinkedIn URL is
already available, skip this search and pass it directly to `GET /company` for one
full profile or to `POST /companies` for a batch lookup.

Exactly one parameter must be provided.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search with relevance scoring
- `domain` — Company domain or full URL
- `linkedin` — LinkedIn company URL
- `crunchbase` — Crunchbase organization URL

Examples:
- `?linkedin=https://linkedin.com/company/stripe`
- `?crunchbase=https://crunchbase.com/organization/notion`

TryfundableSearchDealsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint when the requested result is a set of funding rounds, or when
deal criteria must match any historical round rather than only each company's
latest round. It supports round-level analysis across the full deal history.

For most company-sourcing requests, prefer `POST /companies`: it returns company
metadata together with the full latest deal. Its `latest_deal` filters apply only
to each company's most recent round. For example, use `/companies` for "find AI
companies in San Francisco whose latest round was Seed," but use `/deals` for
"analyze every Seed round announced last year."

Deal records contain full round details, but related companies and investors are
identified by IDs instead of full entity profiles. Use `GET /company?id=...` to
retrieve company metadata and `GET /deals/{id}/investors` to retrieve the full
investor lineup for a returned deal.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific deals by UUID
- `deal` - Filter by deal attributes (financing type, size, date)
- `company` - Filter by company attributes (location, industry, size)
- `investors` - Filter by investor participation (firms or people, by UUID)

TryfundableSearchIndustriesConfig.description:
Use this endpoint before semantic search to resolve a human-readable category into
an exact `INDUSTRY` or `SUPER_CATEGORY` permalink. Agents should not guess permalinks.
If the taxonomy has an appropriate result, use its permalink in the structured
industry filter. Use `search_query` only when the requested niche is not represented
by the taxonomy.

The `name` parameter is required; `type` is optional.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search with relevance scoring (required)
- `type` — Optional filter by industry type: `INDUSTRY` or `SUPER_CATEGORY`
- `industry_type` — Alias for `type`

Examples:
- `?name=artificial intelligence`
- `?name=fintech&type=INDUSTRY`
TryfundableSearchIndustriesConfig.title: TryfundableSearchIndustriesConfig

TryfundableSearchInvestorsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint primarily to resolve a fuzzy investor-firm name or an uncertain
identifier. If a reliable domain or LinkedIn URL is already available, skip this
search and pass it directly to `GET /investor` for one full profile or to
`POST /investors` for a batch lookup.

Exactly one parameter must be provided.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search with relevance scoring
- `domain` — Investor domain or full URL
- `linkedin` — LinkedIn company URL
- `crunchbase` — Crunchbase organization URL

Identifier lookups (`domain`, `linkedin`, `crunchbase`) return `relevance_score: 1`.
Examples:
- `?linkedin=https://linkedin.com/company/sequoia-capital`
- `?crunchbase=https://crunchbase.com/organization/sequoia-capital`

TryfundableSearchLocationsConfig.description:
Use this endpoint to resolve a human-readable city, state, country, or region into
the exact permalink required by location filters on discovery endpoints. Agents
should not guess permalinks. Select the result that matches the user's intended
geography, then pass its permalink to the relevant filter.

The `name` parameter is required; `type` is optional.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search with relevance scoring (required)
- `type` — Optional filter by location type: `CITY`, `STATE`, `REGION`, or `COUNTRY`
- `location_type` — Alias for `type`

Examples:
- `?name=san francisco`
- `?name=california&type=STATE`

TryfundableSearchPeopleConfig.description:
Use this endpoint when the requested result is a list of people.

With `person_type: company`, it returns founders, executives, or employees based on
their current employer. Filters under `company.latest_deal` apply only to that
employer's latest funding round, like `POST /companies`; funding information is used
for filtering but is not included in the returned person record. For example, use
this mode to find founders of AI companies in San Francisco whose latest round was
Series A.

With `person_type: investor`, it applies investment and portfolio filters in the same
way that `POST /investors` does, but returns individual angel investors or lead
partners attached to their firms rather than firm records. Use `POST /investors`
when the desired result is firms, and `POST /deals` when it is funding rounds.

## Request Body Structure
Send a JSON body with up to 4 filter sections plus pagination/sort at the top level:
- `identifiers` - Look up specific people by UUID, LinkedIn, Crunchbase, or Twitter
- `person` - Filter by person attributes (role, contact info, job title, education, prior employers)
- `company` - Filter by current employer attributes (industry, location, funding, IPO status, etc.)
- `investor` - Filter by investor activity (firm, deal characteristics, portfolio companies)

person_type.description:
Restrict results to one population. `company` returns only people with a
current employer (founders, executives, employees). `investor` returns only
people who invest. `any` (default) returns the union — anyone matching the
other filter blocks regardless of population.
person_type.title: Person Type

identifiers.description: Look up specific people by identifier

company.description: Current-employer attribute filters. Setting any field implicitly requires the person to have a current employer.

investor.description:
Filters on the investor entity (firm) and on the person's deal activity.
Setting any field (including any nested `deals.*` field) implicitly requires
the person to be an investor.

sort_by.description:
Sort order. All values are universally accepted — non-applicable values (e.g. `lead_deal_count`
when no investor filter is set) resolve to 0 / null via COALESCE and naturally sort to the bottom (DESC).
Ignored when `company.search_query` or `investor.deals.search_query` is set (results are then
ordered by semantic relevance).
sort_by.title: Sort By

Do NOT use it for stage, location, or funding — apply dedicated filters instead. Results are ordered by relevance and capped at 150 semantic matches.

TryfundableSearchPersonConfig.description:
Use this endpoint primarily to resolve a fuzzy person name or uncertain identifier.
If a reliable LinkedIn URL is already available, skip this search and pass it directly
to `GET /person` for one full profile or to `POST /people` for a batch lookup.

Exactly one parameter must be provided.

**Search types:**
- `name` — Fuzzy name search across both investors AND non-investor people (founders, employees). Returns up to 10 results.
- `id` — Person UUID lookup (returns 0 or 1)
- `linkedin` — LinkedIn person URL or slug
- `crunchbase` — Crunchbase person URL or slug
- `twitter` — Twitter/X URL or handle

`person_type` on each result indicates which pool the row came from
(`investor` wins when a person is in both). For full person detail, use `/person`.

person_type.description:
Optional filter restricting results to one pool. `investor` keeps only
people tracked as investors/angels; `company` keeps only non-investor
people (founders, CEOs, employees). Omit to search both. Applies to
both name and identifier modes — identifier lookups return empty if
the resolved person doesn't match the requested type.
person_type.title: Person Type

TryfundableUnlockPersonEmailConfig.description:
Use this endpoint only when a verified email is explicitly required for an identified
person. Return a verified email for a person identified by UUID, LinkedIn, Crunchbase,
or Twitter/X. Provide one identifier. If multiple identifiers are supplied, the
endpoint uses the first non-empty value in this order: `id`, `linkedin`,
`crunchbase`, `twitter`.

A newly created unlock costs 5 credits. Repeating the request for an email the
same user already unlocked costs 0 credits. Unlock ownership persists across API
keys belonging to that account. Provider attribution is internal and is not returned.

Available on non-trial Pro+, Enterprise, and API plans.
